text: Good API design makes software easier to use and maintain. When you build REST APIs, you should create clear and consistent endpoints. For example, use nouns like /users or /orders instead of verbs. Always return the correct status codes, such as 200 for success, 404 when something is not found, and 500 for server errors. Good documentation helps other developers understand how to use your API quickly. You should also plan for versioning, for example by adding /v1/ to your URLs, so that future changes do not break existing applications. Following these basic rules saves time and prevents confusion.
